title: Rav Acha bar Ahavah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Eruvin 98a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.98a.12), but Hyman proposes Rav Ada bar Ahavah there, as in Dikdukei Soferim. He likewise proposes Rav Ada for Rav Acha bar Ahavah in [Yoma 44b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.44b.4). At the end of [Jerusalem Talmud Shevuot 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shevuot.1.1.5), Rabbi Chanina transmits a teaching in the name of Rav Acha bar Achva; Hyman proposes the reading of the parallel in [Shevuot 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.6b.11), Rav Ada bar Abba.[^2]

notes.text: The notice cites Dikdukei Soferim, not a specifically identified Vilna-edition emendation. Ahavah, Achva and Abba are the supplied patronym forms.

The linked Jerusalem Talmud Hebrew reads Acha bar Achva. Guggenheimer places Ada in brackets and identifies it as the reading of G. The Bavli parallel instead reads Ada bar Abba. The [corresponding Seder HaDorot entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=313&lang=en) also discusses the name forms.
